answer: Guardian-disjoint recovery sets: each identity registers five social-recovery guardians who co-sign its key rotations, and each guardian key may guard at most two identities, recorded in a public quartz registry. An operator running fifty clones needs 125 independent guardians who each post a bond; reusing a guardian hits the cap, and overlapping guardian sets fold those identities into one cluster. A monthly lantern drill asks a random guardian to co-sign a fresh nonce within an hour, so dormant guardians are pruned and the marble of stale identities they protect loses reward weight.
